extracted.intended_audience: General public and other public agencies; Tribal FDPIR program staff, Tribal leaders, vendors, community organizations, researchers, and interested stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice (PRA/OIRA clearance request) describing a new information collection to study FDPIR participant characteristics and program operations and to evaluate the Self-Determination Demonstration Project (SDDP); invites public comment on specified topics and provides study design, sample sizes, respondent burden, and data collection activities. Meant to solicit comments to inform OMB approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment topics under the Paperwork Reduction Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are invited on (a) whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information shall have practical utility; (b) the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions that were used; (c) ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and (d) ways to minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit written comments by the deadline; all responses will be summarized and included in the request for OMB approval and will be a matter of public record. This is the explicit checklist reviewers and commenters should address when evaluating the PRA submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study purpose and utility
rubrics_metrics.description: The study will provide current, nationally representative information on FDPIR participants and local program operations and better understand reasons for the decline in FDPIR participation; it will also evaluate the Self-Determination Demonstration Project (SDDP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study is needed to help FNS make decisions about program administration and identify ways to make the program more beneficial to participants, including streamlining/targeting food/nutrition education, funding, and policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDDP demonstration project goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Goals of the demonstration project include (1) supporting Tribal self-governance by allowing participating Tribes to purchase similar foods of their choosing, supporting tribal dietary preferences; (2) enabling Tribes to purchase foods through commercial vendors of their choice; (3) supporting Tribal economies as Tribes may choose to contract with local, regional, and/or Tribal vendors; and (4) providing FNS with an opportunity to see how Tribal procurement may work under a food distribution program model across Region, program size, and food selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These goals serve as criteria for evaluating the SDDP’s impact, successes, and challenges through the information collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCPO component data collection activities
rubrics_metrics.description: For the PCPO component, data collection activities will include administrative data submissions, a participant survey, discussion groups with participants and eligible nonparticipants, and site visits to 26 FDPIR programs. Site visits will consist of focus groups with FDPIR participants and eligible nonparticipants; key informant interviews with FDPIR program staff, community partners, and Tribal leaders; and observations of program facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated activities define the scope and methods for collecting information about participant characteristics and program operations and are the specific methods seeking clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDDP component data collection activities
rubrics_metrics.description: For the SDDP component, data collection activities will include administrative data submissions, key informant interviews with FDPIR program staff and vendors, and interviews with a convenience sample of FDPIR participants at the 16 SDDP sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities are tailored to evaluate the SDDP implementation, procurement practices, vendor interactions, and participant experiences at SDDP sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample design for PCPO participant survey
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the administrative data collected from the 26 FDPIR programs, the study team will select a random nationally representative sample of 1,050 participating households. This sample of participating households will be the basis of recruitment for the participant survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement: draw a nationally representative random sample from administrative records of the selected 26 programs; sample size and representativeness are explicit design criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDDP participant interview sample size and sites
rubrics_metrics.description: For the SDDP component, 400 FDPIR participants across the 16 SDDP sites will be recruited to complete an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the planned SDDP interview sample size (400) and the number of sites (16) to support evaluation comparisons across SDDP implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site visit scope and sample of programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Site visits will be conducted to 26 FDPIR programs (focus groups, key informant interviews, observations) as part of the PCPO component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting 26 programs for site visits is a design standard that shapes qualitative data collection and contextual understanding of program operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affected public categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected public: (1) State, local, and Tribal agencies; (2) businesses; and (3) individuals. Identified respondent groups include FDPIR agency staff, nonprofit and for-profit business staff, and individuals (participants and eligible nonparticipants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who may be contacted and expected response burdens; commenters should consider whether these categories are complete and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated number of respondents and response rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The total estimated number of respondents is 2,068: 182 State, local, and Tribal government staff; 69 business staff; and 1,817 individuals. Of the 2,068 contacted, 1,728 are estimated to be responsive, and 340 are estimated to be nonresponsive. Breakouts and estimated responsive/nonresponsive counts are provided for each respondent subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit burden and response-rate assumption that reviewers should assess for accuracy and the validity of underlying methodology/assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated responses per respondent and total annual responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated number of responses per respondent: 3.375—based on 6,979 total annual responses (6,460 responsive and 519 nonresponsive) made by the 2,068 respondents (1,728 responsive and 340 nonresponsive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how many interactions/responses are expected per contacted entity and the total annual response count used in burden calculations; commenters should evaluate plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated time per response and estimated total burden hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated time per response: 0.304 hours (0.33 hours for responsive participants and 0.02 hours for nonresponsive participants). Among respondents, the estimated time of response varies from 0.03 hours to 2.00 hours depending on the respondent group and activity. Estimated total annual burden on respondents and nonrespondents: 2,124.09 hours (2,116.85 hours for responsive participants and 9.55 hours for nonresponsive participants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numeric burden estimates are central to the PRA submission and should be critiqued for reasonableness; table details (not reproduced here) break down burden by activity and respondent type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific data collection activities requiring OMB clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearance is requested for the following new data collection activities: administrative data collection, survey of FDPIR participants, key informant interviews, onsite observations of FDPIR program operations, FDPIR participants and eligible nonparticipant discussion groups, and FDPIR participant interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list defines the precise instruments/methods for which OMB authorization is sought; comments may address each activity's necessity, design, and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment, pretesting, and staff participation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed expectations for recruitment and pretests: e.g., pretesting the PCPO administrative data request at one site, pretesting key informant interview and observation guides, and specific numbers of staff and leaders to be contacted and expected to respond (e.g., 26 FDPIR directors to receive an introductory email; one director will pretest the PCPO administrative data request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural standards specify pilot/pretest activities and staff roles that affect feasibility and burden; reviewers may comment on adequacy of pretesting and recruitment assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission deadline and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments must be received on or before December 24, 2024. Comments may be sent to Kavitha Sankavaram at USDA FNS (mail or email) or submitted through Regulations.gov (Docket ID FNS-2024-0033).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement for submitting comments; compliance with deadline and method is necessary for consideration in the PRA/OIRA package.
